input.content:
Beneath the moon the ocean breathes,
a silver tide that softly weaves.
It pulls the shore, then lets it go,
a rhythm only currents know.

The gulls trace arcs above the foam,
where restless waves forget their home.
Salt on the wind, a distant sail,
a whisper caught in every gale.

And when the sun dips down to rest,
the water burns from east to west.
The deep holds secrets none can keep,
and rocks the world, and rocks the world, to sleep.
